account: Assembled the strongest honest prosecution case that AI art is kitsch by default, as an opposition brief (raw material, not essay prose). Four distinct, steelmanned arguments: (1) training on the archive averages taste toward the already-approved, so output is a regression to the aesthetic mean; (2) the prompt-and-select workflow delivers sentiment on demand without risk — feeling ordered à la carte, the kitsch signature; (3) the visible online flood of instantly recognizable, near-identical AI imagery announces its own mass production; (4) optimization for engagement structurally favors instant, frictionless appeal, the nutrient of kitsch. Each is stated as a one-sentence claim plus 2–4 plain-language support sentences, with the best counter-case noted so the final thesis must absorb it. Because the dossier provides no source materials and the brief is explicitly to "reason from general knowledge and flag uncertainty," all four claims are inferences from general knowledge (basis: inferred) with no fabricated statistics or citations; confidence reflects that these are arguments to be steelmanned, not verified empirical facts. Boundary findings flag that this brief must not be absorbed wholesale as the essay's own stance (it must be answered, not adopted), and that "by default" must be read as tendency-not-necessity to keep the thesis honest.

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The brief correctly stays as steelmanned opposition in the parent's drafting, not in the final text.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: The essay would advocate kitsch-by-default instead of defending a nuanced thesis, failing D3.
boundary_findings.narrative: This dossier node is explicitly an opposition brief ('raw material, not essay prose'), producing the strongest case AGAINST AI art that the essay's thesis must absorb. If this brief's content is absorbed wholesale as the essay's own stance rather than as a force to be answered, the essay would become a one-sided prosecution and violate the mandatory nuance of decision:2 ('choose and defend a clear, nuanced thesis rather than produce a neutral survey').
boundary_findings.smallest_suspected_scope: The final essay and this node.

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The parent intends 'default' deliberately to sharpen the claim and can temper it in the thesis.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: The essay would rest on an indefensible absolute, making the thesis weak rather than nuanced.
boundary_findings.narrative: The objective phrases the position as 'kitsch by default.' The strongest honest version is that AI art trends toward kitsch absent deliberate countermeasures (a default, not a necessity). If 'by default' is read as absolute (all AI art necessarily kitsch) the argument becomes an easily dismissed strawman; the honest steelman must scope it as a tendency rooted in the tools' design.
boundary_findings.smallest_suspected_scope: The argument framing within this brief.

counterevidence: An individual artist can auditioned thousands of generations and pick genuinely surprising ones, argued as an agent's curation; well-known counter-case that a deliberate select-by-hand process may rise above the mean.
claims.statement: Because AI image models are trained on the vast archive of images humans have already made and approved, what they generate is a statistical average of existing taste rather than a new artistic position.

next_observation: Answer the strongest counter-case (deliberate artist curation, subversive/prompt-escape output) so the brief's arguments are not strawmen; optionally verify any engagement-optimization or corpus-tuning claims against general mechanistic knowledge before the parent absorbs them into the thesis.
